h1:
Where to Stay in Narathiwat?
10 Hotels We Actually Reviewed
Prices Compared Across 3 Sites!
heroSub: 10 hand-picked Narathiwat hotels across every budget — a 4-star hotel on the Bang Nara River in town, fresh boutique stays in the centre, hotels in Su-ngai Kolok near the railway and the Malaysian border, and a riverside resort in Tak Bai. From roughly ฿650–1,400/night.
introH2: 🕌 Why does choosing the right area in Narathiwat matter so much?
introHtml: Narathiwat is Thailand's southernmost border province, and it's larger than people expect. Stays fall into roughly three areas — Narathiwat town, on the Bang Nara River, close to the clock tower, the central mosque, the markets and Narathat Beach, ideal for those here on business or using the town as a base to explore; Su-ngai Kolok District, a border town next to Malaysia, near the end of the southern railway and the border crossing, suited to travellers connecting by train, crossing the border or running errands at the frontier; and Tak Bai District, near the Taba checkpoint and Wat Chonthara Singhe, for those who want a riverside stay in a quiet border town. Book without checking the area and you can end up driving across districts and wasting time. This guide rounds up 10 hand-picked Narathiwat hotels across every tier — all with real guest reviews, prices compared across 3 sites and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Narathiwat has no metro — the main ways around are a private car, Narathiwat Airport (NAW) or the southern railway, whose terminus is at Su-ngai Kolok. Pick by your itinerary: Narathiwat town sits on the Bang Nara River, close to the clock tower, the central mosque, the markets and Narathat Beach, about 10–12 minutes from the airport — best for business and town sightseeing; Su-ngai Kolok is a border town near the railway station and the Malaysian crossing, good for train connections, border crossings or an overnight stop; and Tak Bai is near the Taba checkpoint and Wat Chonthara Singhe, with a quiet riverside feel. Almost every stay has free parking and pays attention to halal food, so they suit both self-drivers and Muslim travellers.

entries.name: The Imperial Narathiwat Hotel
entries.revCount: 281 reviews · the most among the town hotels · Imperial group
entries.badge: 🏆 The town's flagship · 4-star on the river
entries.mrtTag: 📍 On the Bang Nara River · 250 m to the clock tower
entries.addr: 260 Phichit Bamrung Rd, Bang Nak, Mueang Narathiwat
entries.storyHtml: The Imperial Narathiwat is the town's flagship 4-star hotel, the most-reviewed among the town stays with 281 reviews and a score of 8.5. Part of the Imperial Hotels Group, it sits on the Bang Nara River and was fully renovated in 2023, about 250 m from the clock tower and the central mosque. It has a swimming pool, a poolside bar, a halal breakfast and free parking. Rooms start at ฿900 — a fit for those here on business, for events, or using the town as a base who want full facilities and attentive staff.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a room in the 2023-renovated wing, and if you can, one facing the Bang Nara River for better morning light and a nicer outlook.
pros: Most reviews among the town hotels (281) — plenty of data
Full 4-star facilities — pool, poolside bar, free parking
On the Bang Nara River, walk to the clock tower and central mosque
Halal and southern breakfast; attentive staff
cons: Parts of the building still look dated, awaiting renovation — ask for the new wing
Plain styling, practical rather than boutique

entries.name: Pacinn Narathiwat
entries.revCount: 6 reviews · 9.7, the top score in this guide · newly opened
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Worakhampipit Rd · Bang Nak · in the town centre
entries.addr: 42/1 Worakhampipit Rd, Bang Nak, Mueang Narathiwat
entries.storyHtml: Pacinn Narathiwat is a newly opened hotel with the top review score in this guide, 9.7 (from a base of 6 reviews). Its appeal is its freshness — clean rooms, cute design, a town-centre spot on Worakhampipit Road, free parking and an in-house Japanese restaurant as a bonus. Rooms start at ฿850 — a fit for those who want a brand-new room in the centre of Narathiwat. Worth knowing: it's a new hotel with few reviews so far, and overnight service isn't fully settled yet.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Want a room to sit out in? Take a Deluxe Balcony with its own balcony — only a little more than the standard rooms.

entries.name: Pohnphansa Boutique Hotel
entries.revCount: 25 reviews · 9.0 · every room has a balcony
entries.badge: 🌿 Fresh boutique · every room has a balcony
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ruam Uthit Rd · Bang Nak · near Big C
entries.addr: 77, 79 Ruam Uthit Rd, Bang Nak, Mueang Narathiwat
entries.storyHtml: Pohnphansa Boutique Hotel is a small in-town boutique scoring 9.0 from 25 reviews, with cleanliness as high as 9.4. It has just 16 rooms, renovated in 2022 — spacious, clean and fresh-looking, with soft beds and a private balcony or terrace in every room, some overlooking the garden. There are free bicycles, free parking and Big C about 950 m away, and staff speak Thai, English and Malay. Rooms start at ฿1,000 — a fit for couples or anyone who'd rather have a quiet, fresh boutique in town than a large hotel block.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: With only 16 rooms it fills fast on long weekends — book ahead and ask for a balcony room with a garden view to sit out in.

entries.name: Art Nara Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Khok Khian · near the airport and Narathat Beach
entries.storyHtml: Art Nara Hotel is a boutique with attractive, clean rooms that scores a high 9.1 from 12 reviews. Its strong points are good-looking, fresh rooms and warm service at a starting price of just ฿700. It's in the Khok Khian area on the airport-and-beach side of town, handy for self-drivers and anyone flying in, and it has a Family with Jacuzzi room — a special touch that's hard to find in town. The trade-offs: no in-house restaurant, it's not in the old commercial heart, and the review base is still small.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Travelling as a family? Look at the Family Room or the Family with Jacuzzi — a special option that's rare in Narathiwat.

entries.name: The Bed Kolok Resort
entries.revCount: 12 reviews · 8.6 · Su-ngai Kolok, near the railway

entries.storyHtml: The Bed Kolok Resort is a small, quiet boutique resort and the best value among the Su-ngai Kolok stays, scoring 8.6 from 12 reviews. It's a fit for those in Su-ngai Kolok to connect by train, cross the border or break a journey, who want a clean room, a soft bed and free parking at an easy price. It ranks among the top resorts in town on TripAdvisor. Rooms start at ฿850. The trade-offs: no pool or gym, breakfast costs extra, and it's in a quiet area where you'll head into town for restaurants — best for an overnight stop rather than a long stay.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Connecting on the far-southern railway? Check the train times before booking. It's in a quiet area, so grab some food to keep in your room since restaurants mean a trip into town.

entries.name: Takbailagoon Resort
entries.revCount: 12 reviews · 8.4 · Tak Bai, riverside, near the Taba checkpoint
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Tak Bai · riverside · near the lagoon and Taba checkpoint
entries.addr: 311/2 Moo 7, Che He, Tak Bai District
entries.storyHtml: Takbailagoon Resort is a small riverside resort in Tak Bai, scoring 8.4 from 12 reviews and ranking among the top stays in Tak Bai on TripAdvisor. It's a fit for those in Tak Bai to cross at the Taba checkpoint, visit Wat Chonthara Singhe, or sleep by the river in a quiet border town. Its strong points are the river views, the tasty halal food and the warm welcome, starting at ฿700. The trade-offs: the building is older, the bathroom plumbing isn't always perfect, there's no pool or gym, and it sits in a village away from town — best for a short riverside stay rather than a long one.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Take a Riverside Room facing the Tak Bai River — the water view is the draw here — and try the resort's halal food that many guests praise.

entries.name: Tanyong Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Sopha Phisai Rd · walk to 7-Eleven and Cafe Amazon
entries.addr: 16/1 Sopha Phisai Rd, Bang Nak, Mueang Narathiwat
entries.storyHtml: Tanyong Hotel is a long-standing central hotel that TripAdvisor ranks #1 in Narathiwat, scoring 7.9 from 20 reviews. Open since 1977 and renovated in 2024, it has 84 rooms on Sopha Phisai Road, with a 7-Eleven and a Cafe Amazon just across the street. Its most consistent praise is for staff who are friendly and help beyond expectations. Rooms start at ฿900, with an in-house restaurant and free parking. The trade-offs: the building has age, some rooms are still dated, hot water can be weak at times, and breakfast is basic.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a 2024-renovated room and take a Junior King, which is roomier and some have a city-view balcony. For breakfast, the Cafe Amazon across the road works fine.

The trade-offs: rooms are compact, parking is limited, and facilities aren't as full as a larger hotel.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Travelling with a few people? Take the Triple or Family Deluxe — and if you're driving, check parking when you book, as space is limited.

entries.storyHtml: GreenView Boutique Hotel is the best 4-star option in Su-ngai Kolok, ranked #1 in town on TripAdvisor, scoring 8.0 from 13 reviews. It's a fit for those in Su-ngai Kolok to connect by train, cross the border or run frontier errands who want a clean stay within walking distance of the station and market. Rooms are spacious with cold AC and a good breakfast, starting at ฿1,000. The trade-offs: a few in-room items don't always work fully, it's priced a little above its neighbours, and it's a border town better suited to an overnight stop than a long stay.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Check the in-room items work when you arrive, and during cross-border festival periods book ahead, since it's the town's #1 hotel.

entries.storyHtml: Merlin Hotel Sungai Kolok is the most-reviewed budget stay in this guide, with 318 reviews and a score of 7.7. Its strong points are fresh, clean rooms with cold AC and firm beds, a central spot, and a lighter price than others in the area — from just ฿650. The standout is its 24-hour border shuttle, rare in this town — a fit for those staying over while renewing a visa, crossing into Malaysia or arriving on the far-southern railway. The trade-offs: slow Wi-Fi, wet-zone bathrooms, and no full breakfast.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Crossing the border? The hotel's 24-hour shuttle is handy. Travelling as a couple or group, take the Superior Twin/Family, which is roomier for only a little more.

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Narathiwat hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area is best to stay in Narathiwat?
faq.a: It depends on your itinerary. Narathiwat town suits those here on business or sightseeing — on the Bang Nara River, near the clock tower and Narathat Beach (The Imperial, Pacinn, Pohnphansa, Tanyong, Paksina, Art Nara). Su-ngai Kolok suits train connections, crossing into Malaysia or frontier errands (The Bed Kolok, GreenView, Merlin). Tak Bai suits a riverside stay near the Taba checkpoint and Wat Chonthara Singhe (Takbailagoon).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Narathiwat hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices are very easy on the wallet: budget 2-star stays start around ฿650–920 (Merlin, Paksina); 3-star hotels and boutiques run around ฿700–1,200 (Pacinn, Art Nara, The Bed Kolok, Takbailagoon, Tanyong, Pohnphansa); a 4-star riverside hotel starts at ฿900 (The Imperial) and a 4-star boutique in Su-ngai Kolok runs around ฿1,000 (GreenView). The largest suite, the Imperial Suite, is around ฿3,200.

faq.q: ❓ Where should I stay to connect by train or cross into Malaysia?
faq.a: The far-southern railway terminus and the main border crossing are in Su-ngai Kolok District. Stays near the station and the crossing are The Bed Kolok Resort (quiet boutique resort, ฿850), GreenView Boutique Hotel (4★ boutique, walk to the station, ฿1,000) and Merlin Hotel (budget, ฿650, with a 24-hour border shuttle). For the Taba checkpoint on the Tak Bai side, choose the riverside Takbailagoon Resort.

faq.q: ❓ Do Narathiwat hotels serve halal food?
faq.a: Many do, as Narathiwat places real importance on halal food. The Imperial Narathiwat serves a breakfast buffet with Thai, halal and southern dishes; Takbailagoon Resort in Tak Bai is known for its tasty halal food. Check with the hotel when you book whether the package includes breakfast and offers halal options.

faq.q: ❓ Where should I stay for a riverside room in Narathiwat?
faq.a: In town, The Imperial Narathiwat sits on the Bang Nara River — ask for a Deluxe River View to look out over the water. In Tak Bai District, Takbailagoon Resort is right on the Tak Bai River — take a Riverside Room facing the water, in a quiet riverside setting near the Taba checkpoint and Wat Chonthara Singhe.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Narathiwat hotel?
faq.a: On ordinary weekdays, 1–2 weeks ahead is enough. But low-room-count stays like Pohnphansa Boutique (16 rooms), the in-town boutiques and the popular resorts in Su-ngai Kolok / Tak Bai fill fast on long weekends, holidays and during the town's annual events — book ahead and choose free cancellation in case your plans change.
